newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan allows foreign ships to sail to China.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan allows foreign ships to sail to China.

text.p: Taiwan's Premier Lien Chan has approved a Communication Ministry proposal to let foreign ships sail between Taiwan and China, the ministry said on Tuesday.

"Premier Lien just approved the proposal to allow foreign vessels to sail between Taiwan and China and extend the routes to third areas, in a bid to win more foreign shipping firms to join our Asia-Pacific operation centre plan," a ministry official told Reuters.
"Domestic vessels are not allowed, but Taiwanese-owned, foreign-registered ships were approved," he said.
The proposal still needs a formal cabinet meeting approval to take effect, but with Premier's nod, the proposal has in fact been approved, the official said.

Various shipping firms had expressed hope that Taiwan's planned "offshore shipping centre" can extend to third areas after travelling between China harbours and designated Taiwan offshore transshipment harbours, the ministry has said.
The liberalisation would help expand foreign shipping firms' businesses and boost Taiwan's Asia-Pacific operation centre plan, the ministry has said.

The currently planned rules allow only feeder service by foreign ships and foreign-registered, Taiwan-owned ships to sail between Taiwan and China via a third place, but prohibits extending the routes to third areas, officials said.
Taiwan has banned all direct contacts with China since the two separated after the Chinese civil war ended in 1949. All links must be routed through a third territory.
But recently Taiwan has been exploring ways to ease the ban.

Last year, Taipei devised a plan to set up "offshore transshipment centres" at major ports, allowing cargoes to be transshiped between China and third countries without passing through Taiwan customs. But Taiwan cargoes could not be shipped from the centres to China.
China has not allowed the plan to be implemented, proposing instead to commence direct shipping between the two sides.
